subject: Culture
title: Number Superstitions
description: A quick, practical guide to Number Superstitions.

hook.text: Many Western buildings skip the 13th floor. Many East Asian buildings skip the 4th.

buildup.text: Thirteen's bad luck may trace to the Last Supper. Judas was the 13th guest at the table.

discovery.text: In Chinese, four sounds like 'death.' Hospitals often have no Room 4. Phone numbers avoid it.

twist.text: Eight is lucky in China because it sounds like 'wealth.' A Beijing phone number with all 8s sold for millions.

climax.text: Numbers carry invisible weight. Entire industries bend to accommodate these beliefs.

punchline.text: A digit can raise a price or empty a room.

quiz.question: Why is the number 4 considered unlucky in Chinese culture?
options: It looks like a bad omen
It sounds like the word for death
It was a cursed emperor's number

details.summary: Numbers carry taboo power worldwide. In China and Japan, four sounds like 'death' and is avoided in hospitals, hotels, and phone numbers. In the West, thirteen triggers fear so strong it has a clinical name: triskaidekaphobia. Buildings skip these floor numbers entirely.
details.whyItMatters: Number superstitions cost real money — buildings omit floors, airlines skip row numbers, and product pricing avoids unlucky digits. Irrational fears have deeply rational economic consequences.
takeaways: Four is unlucky in East Asian cultures due to its similarity to 'death'
Many Western buildings skip the 13th floor entirely
Number taboos influence real estate prices and business decisions

faq.question: Why is four unlucky in Asian cultures?
faq.answer: In Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese, and Korean, the word for four sounds nearly identical to the word for death.  Chinese buildings often skip the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 40th-49th floors. Hospitals avoid room four. Gift-giving avoids sets of four. This fear is called tetraphobia.

faq.question: Why is thirteen considered unlucky in Western culture?
faq.answer: Theories include the 13 diners at the Last Supper (Judas being the 13th), Norse mythology where the 13th guest Loki caused tragedy, and the arrest of the Knights Templar on Friday the 13th. Over 80% of high-rise buildings in the US lack a 13th floor, and many hospitals skip room 13.
